<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916627_theRebbe_635" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916627_theRebbe_635__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header with the date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">[B’S”D.</t>
    <t s="1">10 Shevat,</t>
    <t s="2">5713*]</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that turning to holiness above or to the opposite below is called foolishness and heresy.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Above</t>
    <t s="1">(holiness)</t>
    <t s="2">or below</t>
    <t s="3">(to the other side)</t>
    <t s="4">is called foolishness1</t>
    <t s="5">and heresy.2</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the Zohar's wonder at how a soul could sin, and the Alter Rebbe's teaching that a Jew cannot truly be separate from G‑dliness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">How is it possible?3</t>
    <t s="1">And as the Zohar says on the verse “And when a soul will sin,”</t>
    <t s="2">that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Torah wonder: how is it possible that “it will sin”?</t>
    <t s="3">Even though it refers to Nefesh,</t>
    <t s="4">which is the lowest level of the five names of the soul,</t>
    <t s="5">and as the Zohar there specifically emphasizes “Nefesh,” and nevertheless it is wondrous.</t>
    <t s="6">And known is the saying of the Alter Rebbe: “A Jew—whether he wants to or not—cannot be a separate entity from G‑dliness.”</t>
    <t s="7">And only because he does not feel that through a transgression he becomes separate,</t>
    <t s="8">and it seems to him that he is still within Judaism,</t>
    <t s="9">for in truth,</t>
    <t s="10">the 365 negative commandments and all Rabbinic prohibitions,</t>
    <t s="11">since4</t>
    <t s="12">(Tanya ch. 24-25)</t>
    <t s="13">they do not rebel,</t>
    <t s="14">[against] the G‑d of gods,</t>
    <t s="15">that there is another existence.5</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
